current_question: 时间是真实流逝的，还是只是人的感觉？请区分哲学问题和物理学已经能回答的问题，并核对你引用的物理学主张。
target_answer:
这个问句里至少压着四个不同的问题，混在一起就无论证可做。我先拆开，再分别说明哪些是物理学已经（或部分）能回答的、哪些不能，并标注每一条物理主张的核对来源。

## 一、先拆分

1. **世界是否存在一个全局的、不依赖观察者的"现在"，它逐刻向前移动？**（流逝/now 的客观性）
2. **过去与未来之间是否存在客观的方向不对称？**（时间箭头）
3. **在最基本层次上，时间是不是一个基本量？**（时间的奠基地位）
4. **"感到时间在流动"能否被解释为意识与记忆的产物，而不预设真实的流逝？**（经验如何解释）

1、2、3 有很大一部分是物理学能回答或约束的；4 属于认知科学与哲学；而"流逝本身是否实在"是标准的形而上学争点（A 理论／B 理论）。

## 二、物理学已经能回答的部分

**(1) 有没有一个全局的"现在"——相对论给出否定性的强约束。**
按狭义相对论的标准解释：同时性只相对于参考系成立；没有任何参考系在存在论上被优先；因此不存在一种与参考系无关的方式来标出所有"现在"的事件，过去／现在／未来的绝对区分随之不成立（Dyke，《Routledge 哲学百科全书》"Time, metaphysics of" §7，[链接](https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/time-metaphysics-of/v-2/sections/the-a-theory-and-special-relativity)）。
**但要点**：这是对相对论的*标准解释*，不是"已证伪 A 理论"。同一词条指出，有 A 理论者（如 Smith 1993）尝试调和，是否成功是当代在争的问题。所以准确表述是：相对论让"一个全局移动的现在"很难成立，把"物理已证明流逝为假"当作结论则越界了。

**(2) 时间箭头——方向来自边界条件，不来自基本定律。**
《斯坦福哲学百科》"Thermodynamic Asymmetry in Time" 明确写道，这个谜题"通常被认为源于基本物理是时间对称的，更确切说是时间反演不变的"（laws don't care about the direction of time），而热力学的宏观不对称需要一个低熵的初始条件来解释，即 **Past Hypothesis**（[链接](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/time-thermo/)）。也就是说：宏观箭头是真实的，但它不由基本定律单独推出。这个方案是目前的主要解释，其本身地位仍有争论。
这里要纠正一个常被讲错的物理事实——**弱相互作用确实破坏时间反演对称**。核对结果：CP 破坏 1964 年在**中性 K 介子**衰变中被发现；由于 **CPT 定理**（Physics Today 称其"仍是粒子理论的基石定理"），这强烈意味着 T 破坏；2012 年 **BaBar 实验**报告在**中性 B 介子**跃迁中首次取得清晰的、直接的 T 破坏证据（[Physics Today 报道](https://physicstoday.aip.org/news/time-reversal-asymmetry-in-particle-physics-has-finally-been-clearly-seen)）。该报道还记录：1999 年 K⁰ 的"直接 T 破坏"证据被 Wolfenstein 指出无法把 T 与 CP 分开，因而存疑。所以正确说法是：绝大多数基本定律 T 对称，弱相互作用是例外，而这个例外目前并不解释热力学箭头。

**(3) 时间是否基本——未决。**
在正则量子引力中，约束方程（Wheeler–DeWitt 方程）里"根本没有 t"，如何从无时间的量子理论中恢复演化，就是所谓"**时间的难题**"（SEP "Quantum Gravity" §3.2，[链接](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/quantum-gravity/)）。所以"时间是最基本还是派生的"，在最前沿仍是开放问题。

## 三、物理学不能回答、也不该被它替代的部分

- **形式里没有"流逝"。** 物理方程用参数 t 书写，绝大多数解读向过去或未来形式上一致；"流逝／生成"不在形式中出现。但这是**关于形式的事实**，不是"流逝不存在"的证明——缺省既不等于被证明存在，也不等于被证伪。
- **核心哲学争点**：我们的时间经验是否要求世界本身有 A 系列的时态事实。B 理论者的反击是：即使世界是 B 系列（无时态的），经验也能被解释——直接意识的"specious present"极短，加上记忆随时间的累积（Mellor 1998），足以产生"在流动"的印象（Dyke，同词条 §5，[链接](https://www.rep.routledge.com/articles/thematic/time-metaphysics-of/v-2/sections/the-b-theory-and-temporal-experience)）。这正是"只是感觉"这一说法的**最强候选**。
- **但那一步跳跃需要一个额外前提**：B 理论解释的是"为什么我们觉得在流动"，不是"流动是否实在"。要说后者为假，还需要"凡经验可被解释掉的，其对象就不存在"——这个前提本身待论证。

## 四、"只是人的感觉"这个措辞有问题

"只是"偷偷做了价值降级。奥古斯丁《忏悔录》卷十一给出经典的"时间与心灵密切相关"表述："我的心灵啊，我是在你里面度量时间……我度量时间的时候，是在度量印象"，并把时间对应于期望、注意、记忆三种状态（本地《奥古斯丁忏悔录》卷十一）。**但要注意范围**：他谈的是"度量"发生在心灵中、过去与未来在某种意义上"存于心中"，他并未说时间只是错觉，也仍坚持时间的实在（创造在时间中、相对于永恒）。把它读成"时间纯粹是主观幻觉"是扩大了原意。（柏格森的"绵延"与梅洛-庞蒂的"时间性"属于同一传统，但我在本库只读到二手转述，此处不作为依据。）

## 结论

- **物理学能回答的**：有没有全局移动的"现在"（标准解释：没有）；宏观箭头是否真实（真实，但来自边界条件而非基本定律）；时间是否基本（未决）。
- **哲学问题**——那个移动的"现在"、流逝本身是否是世界的一个特征——物理学不直接回答；物理形式里不出现流逝，只能约束、不能裁决。
- **"只是人的感觉"预设了一个额外前提**；B 理论对经验的最佳解释是很强的候选，但它解释的是经验，不是经验对象的存废。就目前可核对的材料看，这场争论**没有共识**。

**核对说明**：上述物理学主张分别来自 Routledge 哲学百科（相对论与 A 理论）、SEP"Thermodynamic Asymmetry in Time"、"Time"、"Quantum Gravity"，以及 Physics Today 的 T 破坏报道，均已实际读取相应段落。我**未**读 McTaggart 原著，也未读 Past Hypothesis 的批评文献（只见到相关论文标题），因此未对它们的内容作断言。

7. The A-theory and special relativity

The other main objection to the A-theory is that it is prima facie inconsistent with the special theory of relativity (see Time §3 ). Given that the special theory is a well-confirmed scientific theory, and thus is very likely to be true, it is incumbent upon any proponent of an A-theory of time to show that the two theories can, in principle, be reconciled. According to the standard interpretation of the special theory, simultaneity does not obtain absolutely, but only relative to a frame of reference (see Relativity theory, philosophical significance of §3 ). It may be the case that e 1 is simultaneous with e 2 relative to one frame of reference, but relative to another, e 1 is earlier than e 2 , and relative to yet another, e 1 is later than e 2 . Furthermore, no one frame of reference is privileged. It follows that there is no frame-independent way of marking out all those events that are simultaneous with the present moment, and thus are themselves present. An event which is present relative to one frame of reference may be past or future relative to another frame of reference, and neither of these frames of reference has a claim to being ontologically privileged. Consequently, there is no absolute (frame-independent) distinction between past, present and future. Furthermore, if presentness confers ontological status on events, then existence itself becomes a frame-relative matter. An event might exist, because it is present, relative to one frame of reference, yet not exist, because it is past or future, relative to another. Some A-theorists (for example, Smith 1993 ) have attempted to reconcile their view with the special theory. Whether such attempts are successful is the subject of much contemporary debate (see Sider 2001 ; Saunders 2002 ; and Balashov and Janssen 2003 ).

5. The B-theory and temporal experience

As well as appealing to the fact that language and thought is tensed (and irreducibly so) to support their theory, A-theorists also appeal to the fact that our temporal experience strongly suggests that time is dynamic. This too can be seen as a challenge to the B-theorist to provide an adequate explanation of why we seem to experience time as flowing if it doesn’t really flow.

There are two features of our temporal experience that need to be explained if the B-theory is true. First, there is the fact that experience seems to occur only in the present. Second, there is the fact that we seem to experience time as flowing. B-theorists generally explain the first of these features by appeal to the fact that our span of direct awareness, or ‘specious present’, is very brief (Dainton 2001 ). Since, at any one time, we are only aware of what is going on in a very limited period of time, it can seem to us that what is located within that very brief time span is all that is really going on. However, just because we are unable to perceive events that are happening at other times does not mean they are not happening at those times.

The B-theorists’ explanation for the apparent experience of temporal passage is often given in terms of the fact that our memories accumulate over time (Mellor 1998 ). Suppose you perceive the hands of a clock showing first 2:00, then 2:15 and then 2:30. These experiences are not totally isolated from each other. Your perception of the clock showing 2:15 is accompanied by a memory of having already perceived it showing 2:00, and your perception of it showing 2:30 is accompanied by a memory of it showing 2:15 while remembering it showing 2:00. According to the B-theorist, our sense of the passage of time is, at least in part, to be explained by the fact that our memories of our experiences accumulate in this way.

When it was discovered in 1957 that the weak interactions of elementary particles are not symmetric under the parity operation P , theorists retreated to the seemingly safe presumption that the combined operation CP remained an inviolate symmetry. (The charge-conjugation operation C replaces all particles by their antiparticles.) But seven years later came a second rude awakening: The decay of neutral K mesons revealed a minuscule but undeniable violation of CP symmetry. So particles viewed in a mirror don’t behave exactly like their antiparticles.

That’s because inviolate CPT symmetry was, and still remains, a bedrock theorem of particle theory.
